approved: Criminal Code Amendment (Keeping Australia Safe) Bill 2026
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would create a new criminal offence for arranging or helping certain people linked to terrorism to enter Australia.

A person could be charged if they organise or facilitate entry of someone who has committed a terrorism offence, intends to commit one, or is a member of a terrorist organisation, unless the foreign affairs and home affairs ministers give written permission beforehand.
The bill would also push back the expiry of the declared areas offence from 7 September 2027 to 7 September 2030.
Creates a new offence for organising or facilitating entry of terrorism-linked persons into Australia.
Requires prior written permission from both the foreign affairs minister and the home affairs minister for the offence not to apply.
Extends the declared areas regime's sunset date by three years to 7 September 2030.
People who organise or facilitate entry into Australia of persons involved in terrorism-related conduct, and Commonwealth authorities.

Mr Taylor [explained that](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debates/?id=2026-03-03.4.2): > *The proposed legislation that we bring before the parliament today has three clear objectives. First, it will end the freelancing of non-government third parties who seek to bring dangerous individuals into the country. It amends the Criminal Code Act 1995 and creates a new offence that would make it a crime to assist the entry into Australia of an individual who has been in a terrorist hot spot, who has links to a terrorist organisation or who has committed terror related offences. They are crucial pre-conditions. In this, the bill seeks to achieve a second objective, which is restoring ministerial accountability. The majority voted against a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?id=2026-04-01.4.2) to agree with the main idea of the bill. In parliamentary jargon, they voted to read the bill for a second time. This means it will not be considered further. ### What is the bill's main idea? The bill was introduced by Tasmanian Senator [Jonathon Duniam](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/tasmania/jonathon_duniam) (Liberal). According to [its homepage](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/s1488), the bill: > *Amends the Criminal Code Act 1995 to: create an offence relating to the unauthorised organisation or facilitation of the entry into Australia of certain persons who have engaged in terrorism-related conduct or who are, or have been, members of a terrorist organisation; and extend the operation of the declared areas offence for a further 3 years to 7 September 2030.*
